chapter: Hutto 1978-79: Specht, Weems and learning to play
title: A Columbia recording session photo and the recording horn
summary: Morehouse describes acoustic recording: music stands hanging from wires, bending the music, and soloists memorizing their solos and going up to the horn.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Now in your album, there is a picture of a recording session I guess at Columbia. Now I know you made records for Columbia in England.
Perchance, was that picture taken in England or do you remember?
I would have to see the music.
The picture is extended out, hung from the ceiling.
And then would come down a music stand. And on that music stand, we would put the music and just stand right up to play it, and bend it a little bit so that the music didn't go right into the stand.
So if you had a solo, you'd maybe go up to the horn.
Yes, that's right. And everybody had to memorize their own solo.
